title: Systematic identification of gene combinations to target in innate immune cells to enhance T cell activation
model: Cas9 mouse bone-marrow-derived dendritic cells, Brie genome-wide and ~2,300-gene secondary knockout libraries, CD86 and PD-L1 FACS sorts
contrast: CD86 low vs high 10% bin, genome-wide screen (2 vs 2); PD-L1 genome-wide (1 vs 1) and both secondary screens (1 vs 1, 2 vs 2) also analyzed
paper_calls: 6 genes at FDR 0.10 in the CD86 genome-wide screen (March1, Cd86, Hspa5, Ubl3, Chd4, 1810013L24Rik); 1 (Cd274) in the PD-L1 genome-wide screen; 95 and 44 in the CD86 and PD-L1 secondary screens, with Cebpb in both
barcs_calls: 6 genes at FDR 0.10 in the CD86 genome-wide screen (6 against the control null); 0 in PD-L1 genome-wide; 120 and 81 in the CD86 and PD-L1 secondary screens
named_hits: Cd86 #2 and March1 #3 (CD86 GW, FDR 0.005); Cebpb FDR 0.036 (CD86 secondary) and #2 (PD-L1 secondary); Med12 #10 (CD86 secondary); Cd274 #2 in PD-L1 GW but not significant
verdict: BARCS reproduces the CD86 genome-wide calls (5 of 6 shared) and nearly all secondary-screen calls including Cebpb and Med12, but calls nothing in the noisy single-repeat PD-L1 genome-wide screen, where MAGeCK calls only Cd274.
